root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Manhattan Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. e3 Bb4

overview: Black pins the c3 knight with ...Bb4 against the Bg5 and ...Nbd7. White usually answers with Bxf6 or Qb3, taking the bishop pair if Black recaptures, and play heads toward ...c5 or ...dxc4. Black keeps a sound structure with queenside play.

white_ideas.idea: Bxf6 and Nge2 to gain the bishop pair
Qb3 or Qa4 hitting the c-pawn

black_ideas.idea: ...Bxc3+ doubles pawns for the bishop pair

typical_structures.structure: QGD structure with d5 and e6 against d4 and e3

character.notes: Tension in the centre and doubled pawns but not forcing.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

level.notes: Plans around the pin and the bishop pair.

character.reason: A pin and some tension but nothing forcing.

level.reason: Needs positional understanding of the pin.

plans.reason: The pin on c3 can lead to doubled pawns and the bishop pair.
